newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bourse to keep CAM suspended.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bourse to keep CAM suspended.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) has decided to continue to prevent trading in the shares of precision engineering group CAM International Holdings Ltd until further notice.
An SES statement, received by Reuters on Saturday, said the financial impact of matters raised in a report by auditors Ernst & Young into the company had still not been clarified.
The report, made public earlier this month, alleged possible breaches of the companies act and penal code by certain CAM directors.
On Friday, CAM said it had accepted the resignation of its managing director, Raymond Chew Chuan Seng, and suspended group financial controller Ng Chee Tiong from all his duties.
The SES said CAM had decided to appoint Ernst & Young to ascertain the financial impact of the alleged transactions.

"As the financial impact of the matters raised in Ernst and Young's report has still not been clarified, the suspension of trading in the company's securities will continue until further notice," the SES said.
The SES said Chew had given a written response to the auditors' report. It said it had not heard from Ng.
Singapore's Business Times on Saturday quoted Chew's response to the SES as rejecting assertions of wrong-doing made against him.
None of those involved in the case were available for comment on Saturday.
